title: Move a boxed mini fridge to a loading spot with a hand truck: plate under, tilt back, roll, stand it up, slide out
instruction: Move the boxed fridge onto the taped loading spot.
context: Delivery drivers, movers and warehouse hand laborers (O*NET 53-7062.00, Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand; 53-7062.04, Stockers and Order Fillers) learn in training to move a heavy carton with a two-wheel hand truck and do it without being told: slide the nose plate fully under the load until it rests against the frame, tilt the truck back until the weight balances over the axle, roll it, stand it up on the spot and slide the plate out. Pushing or dragging an appliance carton across the floor scuffs the floor and the carton and can tip it, lifting a 30 kg carton by hand is a common cause of back injury, and a load that is not seated against the frame slides off the plate when the truck is tilted. Here the carton is too wide for the gripper to grasp, and a hand truck stands upright behind it with its nose plate facing it.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top, which stands in for the floor, at z 0. The scene is at 1:5 scale. A boxed mini fridge, a kraft corrugated carton 10 x 10 x 18 cm and 240 g (a 50 x 50 x 90 cm, 30 kg carton at full size), stands upright with its center at x 30, y 5. Packing tape runs over its top seam, and the face toward the robot has a white product panel with a blue band and two black up-arrows. The carton is wider than the gripper opens (9.4 cm) on every side. A two-wheel hand truck (120 g frame, 100 cm and 15 kg at full size) stands upright behind the carton, facing it, with its axle at x 30, y 20.3, 2.5 cm above the floor. Its frame is red square steel tube: two rails 0.7 x 0.8 cm with centers 7.6 cm apart rising 19.4 cm above the floor, three crossbars, and a loop handle 2.8 cm behind the frame whose black rubber grip (2 x 2 x 6.8 cm) runs across the truck 19 cm above the floor. The frame's front face is 1.8 cm ahead of the axle. A steel nose plate 3 mm thick, 7 cm wide and 7 cm deep, with its front 3 cm beveled to a thin edge and low friction (0.15), lies on the floor at the bottom of the frame and points at the carton, its tip 1.5 cm from the carton's face. Two black rubber wheels with gray hubs, 5 cm across and 1.6 cm wide, with centers 10.4 cm apart, turn freely on the axle. The loading spot is a square of 1 cm yellow floor tape, 16 x 16 cm inside, flat on the floor and centered at x 30, y -13, 18 cm from the carton's start. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole run and scores the end. Five mistakes score 0 and are irreversible, each counted when it lasts 2 control steps in a row (0.1 s at 20 Hz): the carton's footprint (the center of its bottom face) traveled 3 cm in all while not carried on the truck, summed over every stretch where it was not carried, which is pushing, dragging or shoving it with the plate; its lowest corner 1.5 cm off the floor while it is not on the truck (its center more than 2.5 cm from its seat), which is lifting it or letting it slide off the plate; the carton tipped past 75 degrees; both wheels 8 mm above their rolling height with the carton on the truck, which is carrying the truck instead of rolling it; and the carton falling faster than 0.5 m/s (dropped). Seated means the carton's near face within 1.5 cm of the frame's face, its center within 3 cm of the truck's center line and within 1.2 cm of its height resting on the plate, and square to the frame within 12 degrees. Carried means seated, the truck tilted back 10 degrees or more, which lifts the whole plate off the floor, and its wheels on the floor (one within 3 mm of its rolling height, the other within 5 mm). The 3 cm limit (15 cm at full size) leaves room for the plate nudging the carton as it slides under; carrying never resets it, so tilting between pushes does not excuse a shove. Doing nothing, or never carrying the carton, scores 0. Carried but with the carton's center outside the tape at the end scores 0.25. The carton's center inside the tape but the job not finished scores 0.5. Finished means all four bottom corners of the carton inside the tape's inner edge, the carton flat (tilted under 5 degrees, lowest corner within 4 mm of the floor), the plate out from under it (its near face 5 mm past the plate's tip), the truck stood back up within 10 degrees of upright, no gripper closed within 3 cm of the truck or the carton, and both still. Finished scores 1.0 with both arms home and 0.9 with an arm not home. The arms count as home with each tool point within 3 cm of where it started and still, so the aisle is clear. Success is a full score held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0. In a real trial, watch the video for the carton sliding along the floor at any point, lifting, tipping or dropping, for the wheels leaving the floor, and for a roll with the truck tilted less than 10 degrees. Then check that the carton's four base corners are inside the tape's inner edge, that it stands flat with the plate out from under it and the truck upright, and check the arms.
reset_notes: Stand the carton back at its start and the hand truck upright behind it with the nose plate's tip 1.5 cm from the carton. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: 1:5 scale, with masses scaled by volume. The carton is a solid box of uniform density, while a real fridge carton is top-heavy. The wheels collide as spheres of the tire's radius, the nose plate is low-friction steel, and the table top stands in for the floor. The truck is light at this scale, so the arm's grip, not the load's balance over the axle, holds it at its tilt.
